text:
Friendsville community celebrates Maryland's only wild river
FRIENDSVILLE — On Saturday, July 25, members of the community gathered in Friendsville to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the designation of the Youghiogheny as Maryland’s only wild river under the state Scenic and Wild Rivers Program.
A tribute was given to the river and recognition of people and events that have shaped the Yough and its rugged scenic corridor into a key element of the community.
Former State Senator John Bambacus shared how legislative efforts shaped river protections and protected private property in some of the most contentious debates in the river’s history.
The original designation proposed an 11,000-acre protected corridor and allowed for the use of eminent domain to acquire the land from almost 200 private property owners as Swallow Falls was the only state property in the corridor at the time. This push, along with DNR imposed regulations and a growing presence of paddlers, fishermen and hunters interested in a primitive and challenging recreational experience on this wild treasure, led to significant conflict that lasted for decades.
Bruce Bereano made a presentation on behalf of Congressman Steny Hoyer.
“I had the distinct pleasure, privilege, and honor of working for him as his legislative and administrative assistant during the four years he was president of the Maryland Senate,” he said. “... at that time and even still to this date, he is the youngest Senate president in the history of the state of Maryland. In addition … when he completes his term in the congress this January, he will have served as the longest serving congressman in the history of the state of Maryland.”
Bereano stated that he spoke to the Congressman when he was the Senate President about the uniqueness and significance of the Yough River.
“After conversation, he fully agreed — even though his district was in Prince George’s County — he fully agreed we have to save and preserve this river, not only for the magnificence of Garrett County, but showing the importance of Garrett County as part of the state of Maryland.”
He stated that the legislation was put in, even though it was controversial, as most legislation is.
“And with the pressure of Congressman Hoyer … that legislation was passed in 1976 and I thank former Senator Bambacus and the mayor and everyone who was involved,” Bereano said. “It is phenomenal that you’re having the silver anniversary – the 50th anniversary of the Yough and its special status as a wild and scenic river here in the state of Maryland.”
Hoyer then read a letter from the congressman in his absence.
“Please accept my warmest congratulations as you celebrate the 50th anniversary of the designation of the Youghiogheny River as Maryland’s only wild river,” it stated. “This milestone is an excellent opportunity to celebrate one of our state’s great natural treasures and the many people who have worked to protect it over the past five decades. I was proud to help establish these protections during my service in the Maryland Senate, and I am touched to see the enduring legacy of that work. The Youghiogheny remains a remarkable resource for Marylanders, and it is our shared responsibility to ensure that it remains protected for generations to come.”
The letter also noted thanks to Bereano for “his steadfast advocacy and for helping ensure that this important anniversary is recognized. His longstanding commitment to the Youghiogheny River has helped keep its legacy alive.”
The free event was organized at the Friendsville Town Park by volunteers Madi Mori, Jesse Whittemore, and Steve Storck of Swallow Falls have organized a free event at Friendsville Town Park. The event included the band Aurora Celtic, food vendors, and a beer garden, with all proceeds benefitting the local Mountain Watershed Association. Music was also presented by Jesse “Shimmy” Shimrock, Dirk Schwenk and The Meaderthals.
